create.name: OECD TKS2024｜评价方法（无计分）｜教师自评｜ISCED2英文
create.description: Original English TKS 2024 contextual item block; unscored, not a knowledge test or an OECD factor score. Version 1.0.0. OECD (2024), “Teacher Knowledge Survey (TKS): Teacher Questionnaire”, https://www.oecd.org/content/dam/oecd/en/about/programmes/edu/talis/tks2024questionnaires/TKS_MS_instrument(long)_withSEnames-REDACTED.pdf
create.instruction:
The <class> that we would like you to respond to is the first <ISCED 2011 Level 2> <class> that you taught in this school after 11 a.m. last Tuesday. Please note that if you do not teach a <class> at <ISCED 2011 Level 2> on Tuesday, this can be a class taught on a day following the last Tuesday. In the questions below, this <class> will be referred to as the <target class>.

EduK12 adaptation: selected original English TKS contextual questions for unscored teacher reflection. Numeric source response codes identify categories, not points. You may leave an item unanswered. Keep the same target class across modules. These forms do not measure pedagogical knowledge, competence or observed teaching quality. Q27 refers specifically to lessons over the past week.

OECD (2024), “Teacher Knowledge Survey (TKS): Teacher Questionnaire”, https://www.oecd.org/content/dam/oecd/en/about/programmes/edu/talis/tks2024questionnaires/TKS_MS_instrument(long)_withSEnames-REDACTED.pdf

addItem.formLabel:
How often do you use the following methods of assessing student learning in the <target class>?
Please mark one choice in each row.

formDefinition.prompt:
How often do you use the following methods of assessing student learning in the <target class>?
Please mark one choice in each row.

rows.label: I administer an assessment at the end of a unit or block of lessons.
I give a <mark, e.g. numeric score, letter grade, smiley face> to communicate to students how they performed in relation to their classmates.
I provide oral or written feedback to indicate areas for improvement.
I ask students to assess their own progress.
I observe students when working on particular tasks and provide immediate feedback.
I use assessments to check whether students have learned the material presented.

addItem.formLabel:
Thinking about your teaching in the <target class>, how often do you perform the following actions?
Please mark one choice in each row.

formDefinition.prompt:
Thinking about your teaching in the <target class>, how often do you perform the following actions?
Please mark one choice in each row.

rows.label: I consider students’ prior knowledge and needs when planning a lesson.
I point students to different materials for learning depending on their needs.
I change my way of explaining when a student has difficulties understanding a topic or task.
I adapt my teaching methods to students’ needs.
I ask questions at various difficulty levels to check students’ understanding of the subject matter.

Please mark one choice in each row.

formDefinition.prompt:
Thinking about your teaching in the <target class>, how often do you perform the following actions?
Please mark one choice in each row.

rows.label: I let students review multiple examples to practice the steps involved in a procedure or skill.

I prepare students for difficulties that can occur while practicing a procedure or skill.
I let students practise similar tasks until I know that every student has understood the subject matter.

addItem.formLabel:
Teaching is a complex activity with often competing goals. To what extent have the lessons you taught over the past week in the <target class> achieved the following aims?
Please mark one choice in each row.

formDefinition.prompt:
Teaching is a complex activity with often competing goals. To what extent have the lessons you taught over the past week in the <target class> achieved the following aims?
Please mark one choice in each row.

rows.label: Presenting the content in a comprehensible way
Engaging students in work that challenges them
Providing students with feedback to support their learning
Offering students opportunities to practice what they learned
Adapting teaching to meet the different needs of students
Helping students to manage their own emotions, thoughts, and behaviour
Managing student behaviour
